facts: Three applications were filed under Article 226 of the Constitution before the High Court of Bombay by the respective appellants before us challenging the rejection of their highest offers in response to invitation by public tender without assigning any reason for the same as arbitrary, unconstitutional and contrary to rule of law.

The respondent a Government company within the meaning of section 617 of the Companies Act has been constituted as the New Town Development Authority under sub-s. (3A) of s. 113 of the Maharashtra Regional Town Planning Act, 1966.

According to the appellants the normal practice adopted by the Corporation is to invite tenders for the disposal of specified plots which the Corporation chooses to assign according to the terms and conditions for lease of plots for mercantile use.
issues: Whether the respondent's rejection of the highest offers without assigning any reason is arbitrary, unconstitutional and contrary to rule of law.
Whether the respondent has a naked and unguided power to reject the highest offers without assigning any reason.
petitioner_arguments: The procedure is contrary to the requirement of rule of law and therefore, cannot be sustained.

The State is 'State' within the meaning of Art. 12 and in its dealings with the citizens of India it would be required to act within the ambit of rule of law and would not be permitted to conduct its activities arbitrarily.
respondent_arguments: There is no allegation of mala fides in the conduct of respondent No. 1 in refusing to accept the highest offer.
The State is certainly entitled to look for the best deal in regard to its properties.
court_reasoning: We do not find it difficult to agree with Mr. Dwivedi's submissions that respondent No. 1 is 'State' within the meaning of Art. 12 and in its dealings with the citizens of India it would be required to act within the ambit of rule of law and would not be permitted to conduct its activities arbitrarily.

The State has descended into the commercial field and giant public sector undertakings have grown up, the stake of the public exchequer is also large justifying larger social audit, judicial control and review by opening of the public gaze;
